_readme: Task cards. Only the lead writes this file. "passes" is set by CI or the lead, never by a worker. Flags: star = demo path, purple = needed for Veda by 9:30 AM. Intent is copied word for word from docs/plan.md section 7. read_first lists docs a worker should read before starting (shown in section 4.4 of the brief). progress says what already exists from the walking skeleton.

tasks.title: repo + ownership
tasks.why: Everyone must know which folders are theirs before anyone starts.

plain: ownership.json lists every lane and every lead-only path
Branch naming rule is written down
comms branch exists with the agreed file layout

tasks.title: rules, commands, docs
tasks.why: Every laptop gets the same rules and the same five commands.

plain: /checkin, /start, /explain, /ask, /handback exist as skills
CLAUDE.md stays about 100 lines or less
Brief and update templates match the spec

tasks.title: guardrails + CI
tasks.why: Hooks warn early; CI is the real gate for ownership, secrets, attribution and file size.

plain: A bad edit outside a lane is blocked or flagged
CI checks ownership, no AI attribution, file size, secrets and contract schemas
CI finishes in under 5 minutes

tasks.title: contracts + fake data
tasks.why: Lanes build in parallel against agreed data shapes and fake data.

plain: Every contract is a JSON Schema with a version field
Every contract has fake data in fixtures/ that validates
Test list written in plain English and approved by a human before test code

tasks.title: setup checks
tasks.why: New laptops must be ready without anyone reading raw errors.

plain: setup-check.ps1 and setup-check.sh report each tool with the exact install command when missing
.gitattributes prevents Windows line-ending bugs

tasks.title: walking skeleton
tasks.why: Veda starts at ~10 AM; everything she needs must already work end to end on fake data.

plain: Upload, fake analysis, sheet music, play/pause/tempo/pitch buttons, command system and a TouchDesigner message all work on fake data
L1, L6, L2, C1/C2, B1/B4 and D1-D3 are ready for Veda
Every later merge keeps the skeleton working

tasks.title: email relay
tasks.why: Lets people use the system by email and lets the main laptop reach a human who is away.

plain: Sends only to the allowed addresses kept in the private file
ask-human emails after 3 minutes unanswered; first answer wins
[MUSIC] commands work by email; overrides need CONFIRM <code>

out_of_scope: Sadie must type the Gmail app password herself

tasks.title: Vultr budget watcher
tasks.why: Vultr has a $100 credit on a real card; we must not go over it.

plain: Checks the balance every 30 minutes with a key only the script reads
Alerts at $50, $75 and $90 spent (emailed through the relay, on screen until it exists)
Can only read from Vultr; the command guard blocks creating, changing or deleting resources
Never prints the API key

out_of_scope: Creating or deleting any Vultr resource

tasks.title: command system + mapping engine
tasks.why: Buttons, voice, gestures and email all go through one command path that Veda can edit in plain text.

plain: Reads mappings.yaml and applies it
Editing the file takes effect instantly (hot reload)
Smoothing, cooldown_ms, min_confidence, range, step and only_while all work
A bad line is skipped and shown as a friendly error; the app keeps running
Two commands fighting over the same signal in the same mode give a warning

out_of_scope: Building signal detectors (lanes B and C)
tasks.progress: Skeleton merged and tested (rules, smoothing, cooldown, arming, friendly errors, instant reload, conflict warnings). Remaining: tuning with real camera and mic, and Veda's final command list.

tasks.title: Command Lab
tasks.why: Veda needs to see what the app senses and what each command does while she designs.

plain: Live camera view with tracking drawn on top
A live meter for every signal
Every control with its current value
Each command lights up when it fires

out_of_scope: New signals or controls from other lanes (ask the main laptop)
tasks.progress: Skeleton merged and tested (live camera with tracking overlay, a meter per signal, controls, rules that light up, and a no-camera test panel). Remaining: look and layout, real-device checks.

tasks.title: Veda designs the play + create commands
tasks.intent: Veda designs the play + create commands
tasks.why: Veda owns command design and may change any design detail of her part.

plain: Final command list for play and create modes is in mappings.yaml with comments
Voice-command arming decision is made
Final list of tracked body parts is decided

tasks.progress: Not started. The starter mappings are in web/src/modules/mappings/mappings.yaml and the Command Lab lets her try them with no camera.

tasks.title: datasets
tasks.why: Analysis and training need test music; nothing large goes in git.

plain: A usable set of public-domain or self-recorded music exists in Vultr storage
No audio or datasets are committed to git

tasks.title: tempo + key
tasks.why: Upload analysis starts with tempo, key and time signature.

plain: Given audio, returns tempo, beats, key and time signature matching the song-analysis contract
Works on the demo songs

tasks.progress: Built and tested on synthetic audio: tempo (within 0.01% on clean beats), beats, 3/4 vs 4/4, key (24 keys right), about 5 s for 3 minutes. Remaining: try real recordings (a human with a few songs).

tasks.title: segmentation
tasks.why: Separating the part before transcribing avoids messy sheet music.

plain: Isolates the requested part from a full song
Output feeds sheet-music generation

tasks.progress: Light version built and tested on generated drum mixes: when a song looks like many instruments, the drums are taken out (harmonic/percussive split) and the melody is read a second time; the second result is used only if clearly better, otherwise the first result and the full-mix warning stay. Drum-heavy mixes went from about 0.3-0.7 to about 1.0 precision. It does not help when a chord is as loud as the tune, and a real band mix still gets the warning. Real separation of instruments (a heavy model) is not built. Remaining: try real songs (a human with a few).

tasks.title: sheet music
tasks.why: The learner needs notes to play along with.

plain: Produces concert-pitch note events quantized to the tempo grid
Sheet music renders; beginner mode shows note letters
Falls back to note letters if the notation is messy

tasks.progress: Built and tested on synthetic audio: melody from a single line (pYIN), octave and tuning fixes, quantized to beats, about 0.99 precision and recall. Remaining: real instruments and voices; a full band mix has its drums taken out first (A3 light) and still gets a warning when it looks like many instruments.

tasks.title: frozen test set
tasks.why: A fair, leak-free way to judge any model.

plain: Held-out split by piece and performer, frozen
Scoring uses mir_eval note-onset F1 against basic-pitch
Results are logged to files

tasks.title: custom PyTorch model
tasks.why: Optional upgrade over pretrained models.

plain: Only swapped in if it beats the basic-pitch baseline on the frozen test set
Leakage review done before each training run

tasks.title: mic + pitch
tasks.why: Everything live (feedback, snap/clap, create mode) starts from the mic.

plain: Mic input works in Chrome
Detected pitch and note onsets are produced as performance events
Runs without freezing the page

tasks.progress: Skeleton merged: mic, pitch (pitchy), notes, onsets, loudness, fake mode. Remaining: check with a real mic.

tasks.title: compare user to song (+ timing calibration)
tasks.intent: compare user to song (+ timing calibration)
tasks.why: Feedback needs the learner compared to the song; calibration removes device latency.

plain: Clap calibration produces one shared latency offset
User notes are compared to the song; tempo feedback works (demo focus)

tasks.progress: Built and tested: clap calibration, matching played notes to the song (works at any speed), rule-based feedback with tempo, bars, pitch. Remaining: check on a real mic with headphones; tune thresholds in audio-live/practice/config.ts.

tasks.title: feedback + Gemini
tasks.why: Instant rule-based feedback, with Gemini coaching filling in after.

plain: Rule-based feedback shows instantly
Gemini coaching fills in afterward; the Gemini key stays on the server
Canned coaching works with no network

tasks.progress: Done: instant rule-based feedback, Gemini coaching through the server (checked with a real call, about 1.3 s) with a built-in fallback, practice panel, history trend.

tasks.title: keywords + snap/clap
tasks.why: Voice and clap/snap are core command signals.

plain: Snap and clap detected as moment signals
Keywords only listen when armed by a gesture so the instrument does not trigger them

tasks.progress: Skeleton merged: snap and clap classifier, keywords armed by left fist (Web Speech). Remaining: tune thresholds with real snaps and claps.

tasks.title: tracking
tasks.why: Hand and head tracking drives play-mode control.

plain: MediaPipe runs in a background worker at about 15 fps
Hand height/x and head signals are published as signals
Page stays responsive

tasks.progress: Skeleton merged: MediaPipe hands and face in a worker at about 15 fps, signals and landmarks, fake mode. Remaining: check with a real webcam (left/right labels, thresholds).

tasks.title: basic gestures
tasks.why: Gestures are the moment signals commands use.

plain: Fist, open palm, hand up, pinch, two-hand distance, head tilt, nod and drum-hit are detected and listed in the signal catalog

tasks.progress: Skeleton merged: fist, open palm, raised, pinch, nod, drum hit, head tilt, hand distance (tested on synthetic landmarks). Remaining: tune on real people.

tasks.title: TouchDesigner connection
tasks.why: Visuals must react to music and hands.

plain: A small local relay forwards td-message data to TouchDesigner (browsers cannot send UDP/OSC)
Audio features and hand data arrive in TouchDesigner

tasks.progress: Skeleton merged: sender at 30 fps and a local relay to TouchDesigner (OSC and WebSocket, origin check). Remaining: test in TouchDesigner, the visuals themselves (human).

tasks.title: hum → notes
tasks.why: Create mode starts with the player humming a melody.

plain: A hummed melody becomes note events

tasks.progress: Skeleton plus quality merged: octave jump fix, tuning offset, optional snap to key, 0.97 precision and recall on synthetic hums. Remaining: real microphone.

tasks.title: instruments
tasks.why: Hummed notes need to sound like an instrument.

plain: Notes play back through a selectable instrument sound

tasks.progress: Skeleton merged: piano, synth, bass, pluck, drums and effects (Tone.js). Remaining: listen and polish.

tasks.title: layers + loops
tasks.why: Layers and loops turn a hum into a beat.

plain: Add layers, record and stop loops, per-layer volume

tasks.progress: Skeleton merged: layers, count-in, 2-bar loop, beat, volume and effects. Remaining: listen, timing offset with a real mic.

tasks.title: save + replay
tasks.why: Creations should be saved and played back.

plain: A created track can be saved and replayed

tasks.progress: Done: save a track and play it back later, even after a reload; falls back to this computer when the server is away.

tasks.title: playback (tempo without pitch change, pitch shift)
tasks.intent: playback (tempo without pitch change, pitch shift)
tasks.why: Slowing down to practice without changing pitch is the core of Learn and Play mode.

plain: Tempo 0.5-1.5 without changing pitch
Pitch shift of plus or minus 12 semitones
Volume, loop and loop section work
The time-stretch library was tested early

tasks.progress: Skeleton plus hardening merged: tempo and pitch independent (measured), worklet output (no dropouts in real Chrome), bypass at normal speed, loop crossfade, position within about 6 ms of what is heard. Remaining: listen on real speakers.

tasks.title: app shell
tasks.why: Everything else plugs into the app shell and sheet view.

plain: Upload, song view and sheet music display work
Modules plug in without editing each other

tasks.progress: Merged: shell, song loader, sheet music, camera preview on every tab, Practice panel, history, optional login. Remaining: the real design (F1).

tasks.title: server + Tiger Data + Auth0
tasks.why: Server, history storage and login for sponsors; Auth0 is last and can be switched off.

plain: Server runs with Tiger Data for songs, analyses and practice sessions
Auth0 login works and can be switched off

tasks.progress: Merged: upload, real analysis hook (see A2/A4), saving songs, sessions, feedback and creations (memory or Tiger Data), optional Auth0 login on server and website. The real Tiger Data database is connected and the tables are created (11 statements, safe to repeat); a real round trip (song, analysis, practice session and samples, feedback, saved track) worked and was cleaned up. Remaining: restart the running server so it uses the database, try login against the real Auth0 tenant.

tasks.title: deploy
tasks.why: Public demo hosting plus a local demo mode for bad Wi-Fi.

plain: Deployed on Vultr
Local demo mode works with cached results and canned coaching

tasks.progress: Files only, nothing created on Vultr: deploy/ has a plain-language runbook with the cost estimate (about $10 a month, $1 to $2 for 3 to 4 days, from memory: verify on the Vultr page), a setup script and an update script for the new Ubuntu server, a Caddy config (HTTPS, the website, /api proxy) and a service file. Checked locally: the website builds, the production-style server answers, the scripts parse (node deploy/check-local.mjs). NOT tested: any real server, the HTTPS certificate, the Caddy file, camera over HTTPS, login on the domain. Needs a human yes with the cost, the domain name, and the code on GitHub main before it can be used.

tasks.title: the real look (after inspiration arrives)
tasks.why: The app must not look AI-generated.

plain: Design inspiration from a human is applied across the app

out_of_scope: Starting before design inspiration is provided
tasks.progress: Three 3D mockup directions made and shown to Lalitha (A Firefly Marsh, B Glass Hall, C Paper Reef; Learn and Play screens each) as real WebGL scenes with the app's real labels. Waiting for her pick (or a mix) and any inspiration, then a helper builds it in web/src/ui and web/src/styles. The source of the mockups is in scratch/design-mockups (not in git). Needs three.js added to web/package.json by the lead.
